Batch 94 Forensic Discoveries

Batch 94 recovers and dates 16 extraordinary historical broadcasts spanning legendary one-man stage performances, dramatic radio masterworks, Holocaust survivor eyewitness accounts, post-war European reportage, presidential archive recordings, aviation tragedy ceremonies, voice acting virtuosity, linguistic etymology, and swing broadcasts: 3 hilarious stories from Groucho Marx's sold-out Carnegie Hall tour An Evening with Groucho (1972; including Uncle Herman the chiropodist, W.C. Fields spiking Baby LeRoy's bottle, and World War I vaudeville tours in Toronto), Orson Welles starring in Joseph Conrad's Heart of Darkness alongside Robert Young on This Is My Best (1945), British Channel Islands schoolteacher Harold Osmond Le Druillenec's harrowing first-person BBC testimony following his liberation from Bergen-Belsen concentration camp (June 1945), Edward R. Murrow's classic CBS report on occupied Germany ('Delayed Action War'), the live German and American funeral service broadcast from Lakehurst Naval Air Station following the 1937 Hindenburg disaster, Mel Blanc doing Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck, and Porky Pig for the Veterans Administration on Here's to Veterans (1948), Basil Rathbone explaining the origins of 'Saxophone' and 'Stoic' on Word Detective (1959), Franklin D. Roosevelt's 1920 vice-presidential acceptance address, Frank Sinatra on To Be Perfectly Frank (1953), Bobby Hammack's quartet (1955), and 2 big band broadcasts from AFRS Swingtime featuring Bob Crosby, Harry James, Mel Tormé, and Duke Ellington (1944).
